questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if the appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follows(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

1. No bottle is a pen

2. All jugs are bottles.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some jugs are pens.

II. No jug is pen

III. Some bottles are jugs.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Conclusion III and either conclusion I or II follow.
All conclusions I, II and III follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/627d417fbc2723678d237223c27d330ec4c1251de6c00f230821555b7f469d1c.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some jugs are pens → False (All jugs are bottles and No bottle is a pen)

II. No jug is pen → True(All jugs are bottles and No bottle is a pen)

III. Some bottles are jugs → True (All jugs are bottles)

Hence, only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.question: In a class of 100 students, every student has passed in one or more of the three subjects, i.e History, Economics and English. Among all the student, 24 students have passed in English only, 14 students have passed in History only 11 students have passed in both English and Economics only, and 12 students have passed in both English and History only. A total of 50 students have passed in History. If only 5 students have passed in all three subjects, then how many students have passed in Economies only?
questions.solution:
Total no. of students in the class = 100

No. of students passed in English only = 24

No. of students passed in History only = 14

No. of students passed in both English and Economics only = 11

No. of students passed in both English and History only = 12

No. of students passed in History = 50

No. of students passed in all three subjects = 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d51b8d7a5e8ebd2d2e902b7830d7bc5c4e847611e44cecf1681373d95810b270.png] 

No. of students who passed in Economics only = 100 - (50 + 24 + 11) = 100 - 85 = 15.

Hence, 15 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132
questions.solution:
Given equation: 28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132

1) × and -; 32 and 34

Interchanging according to the option

 28 × 34 ÷ 2 – 8 + 32

= 28 × 17 – 8 + 32

= 476 – 8 + 32

= 508 – 8

= 500 ≠ 132

**2) + AND -; 32 and 34**

**Interchanging according to the option**

**28 + 34 ÷ 2 × 8 – 32**

**= 28 + 17 × 8 – 32**

**= 28 + 136 – 32 **

**= 164 – 32 **

**= 132**

3) + and -; 28 and 32

Interchanging according to the option

32 + 28 ÷ 2 × 8 – 34

= 32 + 14 × 8 – 34

= 32 + 112 – 34

= 144 – 34

= 110 ≠ 132

4) × and -; 8 and 2

Interchanging according to the option

28 × 32 ÷ 8 – 2 + 34

= 28 × 4 – 2 + 34

= 112 – 2 + 34

= 146 – 2

= 144 ≠ 132

Hence, + AND -; 32 and 34 is the correct answer

questions.question: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.solution:
Distance between A and B = 428 km

Speed of first train = 48 km/hr

Distanced covered in 20 min by first train = 48/60 × 20 = 16 km

Remaining distance = 428 - 16 = 412 km

Speed of second train = 55 km/hr

If both train running opposite train, then relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/hr

Time = distance/speed = 412/103 = 4 hr

∴ Train meet each other = 6 : 00 + 0 : 20 + 4 : 00 = 10 : 20 a. m

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement.**

Amit has __the good command on__ English as he was born and brought up in England.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **"a good command over".**
 
• In English, when you want to express proficiency in a language, you use the preposition** "over"** or** "of" after "command".**
 
• So the **phrase should** be "Amit has a good command over English" or "Amit has a good command of English".

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is*: "Amit has a good command over English as he was born and brought up in England."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"A better command of" - **This would be correct if we were comparing Amit's command of English to someone else's. But the sentence does not make any such comparison.
 
• **"The best command in" -** This is not correct. The phrase is either "command of" or "command over". The word "best" implies comparison, but the sentence does not compare Amit's command of English to anyone else's.

questions.question:
**Select the indirect narration of the given sentence.**

He said to me, "What time do the banks open and close?"

options.text: He asked me what time do the banks open and close.
He said me what time did the banks open and close.
He asked me what time the banks opened and closed.
He wanted to know what time the banks open and close.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3 i.e. He asked me what time the banks opened and closed.**

The original sentence has a question mark, thus the indirect sentence **should have a verb like 'asked' or 'questioned**', thus option 2 and 4 are incorrect because they **use different verbs**. option 1 cannot be used as reported speech is supposed to have** verbs in the past tense, but option 1 uses the present tense.**

**Thus, the correct answer is option 3. **
